skill.name: python-typing-patterns
skill.description: Python typing reference for adding type hints, generics, protocols, overloads, runtime validation, and strict mypy or pyright checks.
skill.summary: Add and validate modern Python type hints with practical examples for mypy, pyright, protocols, overloads, and runtime validation.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives after reviewing the referenced files. The skill contains Python typing documentation, sample configuration, and a local type-checking helper script; no prompt injection, credential theft, data exfiltration, or malicious system behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples resemble network calls and command usage to pattern scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label code blocks as examples and clarify that URLs such as api.example.com are placeholders that users must replace intentionally.

remediation.issue: The shell helper creates a temporary pyright configuration file.
remediation.suggestion: Add a trap to remove the temporary file on interruption so cleanup is reliable in all exit paths.

content.value_statement: Python type annotations can be hard to apply consistently across real projects. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for safer typed Python code.
actual_capabilities: Shows modern Python 3.10+ type annotation patterns for functions, collections, unions, and optional values.
Explains TypeVar, Generic, ParamSpec, TypeVarTuple, Self, and variance patterns.
Provides Protocol and structural typing examples for flexible interfaces.
Demonstrates overload patterns with Literal, optional parameters, generics, and async functions.
Includes mypy and pyright configuration examples for strict type checking.
Includes runtime validation examples with Pydantic, typeguard, and beartype.
limitations: It is a reference skill, not an automatic type migration tool.
Some examples require Python 3.11 or newer features.
It does not guarantee that project-specific third-party libraries have complete type stubs.
The included shell script depends on locally installed mypy or pyright.

use_cases.title: Annotate new Python services
use_cases.description: Use the reference patterns to add clear function signatures, collection types, and strict checker settings before code grows complex.

use_cases.title: Modernize legacy type hints
use_cases.description: Apply unions, TypedDict, Protocol, and TypeGuard patterns to make existing Python code easier to check and maintain.

use_cases.title: Teach practical Python typing
use_cases.description: Use the examples as structured explanations for teams learning mypy, pyright, generics, overloads, and runtime validation.

prompt_templates.title: Add basic annotations
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a small function or module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Python type hints to this module using modern Python 3.10+ syntax. Keep the changes simple and explain any uncertain types.

prompt_templates.title: Choose safer collection types
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for API boundaries or shared helpers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these function signatures and suggest better collection types, such as Sequence, Mapping, Iterable, TypedDict, or Protocol.

prompt_templates.title: Configure strict type checking
prompt_templates.scenario: Project setup with mypy or pyright.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a practical mypy and pyright configuration for this Python project. Explain which strict settings should be enabled first.

prompt_templates.title: Design advanced typed APIs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced work on libraries, decorators, or polymorphic APIs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use TypeVar, ParamSpec, Protocol, overload, and runtime validation where appropriate to make this API type-safe without overcomplicating it.

output_examples.input: A function accepts either text or bytes and should return the same kind of value.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend overload signatures for each input type, followed by one implementation that handles all accepted cases.

output_examples.input: A project wants stricter type checking but has untyped tests and third-party packages.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest strict defaults, targeted test overrides, missing-import settings, and separate mypy or pyright configuration examples.

output_examples.input: A service needs validation for request dictionaries at runtime.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest TypedDict for static shape and Pydantic TypeAdapter or BaseModel patterns for runtime validation.

best_practices: Start with function boundaries, public models, and configuration before annotating every internal variable.
Use Protocol for behavior-based interfaces and TypedDict for dictionaries with known keys.
Run mypy or pyright regularly so type annotations stay accurate as code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use Any to silence errors unless the value truly has an unknown type boundary.
Do not add overloads when a simple union or generic type explains the API clearly.
Do not rely on runtime validation alone when static type checks can catch issues earlier.

faq.question: Does this skill write type hints automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and guidance that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can apply when editing Python code.

faq.question: Which Python versions are supported?
faq.answer: Most examples target Python 3.10 or newer. Some patterns, such as Self and TypeVarTuple, need Python 3.11 or newer.

faq.question: Does it support both mypy and pyright?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes configuration examples and command guidance for both type checkers.

faq.question: Can it help with Pydantic?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Pydantic v2 examples for models, validators, function arguments, and TypeAdapter validation.

faq.question: Is this useful for existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The gradual typing guidance helps teams add stricter checks in phases without blocking all legacy code at once.

faq.question: Does it execute network requests?
faq.answer: No. Network-looking snippets are documentation examples. The included helper script only runs local type checkers.
